Pointing to a woman, Nirmal said, "She is the daughter of my wife's grandfather's only child". How is the woman related to Nirmal ?
E is the daughter of P who is the husband of the only daughter-in-law of K ? How is E related to K?
solution: X is the daughter-in-law of K and wife of P, so P is K's son. Hence, E is the granddaughter of K.

In each question below, given two statements followed by four conclusions numbered I to IV. Consider the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts. Determine which conclusions logically follow from the given statements.

**Statement:**
All roads are bricks.
Some bricks are ropes.
All ropes are doors.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some roads are doors.
II. Some doors are bricks.
III. Some roads are not doors.
IV. All doors are ropes.
options: Only I, II and III follow.
Either I or III and II follow.
Either I or III and IV follow.
solution:
From the Venn diagram: I – possible only; II – follows (some bricks are ropes, all ropes are doors); III – possible only; IV – does not follow.

I and III form a complementary pair, so either I or III follows, and II follows.

**Conclusions:**
(I) Some aeroplanes are chairs.
(II) Some chairs are aeroplanes.
(III) Some chairs are trains.

solution: (I) Some aeroplanes are chairs – possible only. (II) Some chairs are aeroplanes – possible only. (III) Some chairs are trains – follows. (IV) Some trains are aeroplanes – follows.
